Great coverage of the Faroe islands but you didn't mention one detail; The place is amazingly clean and tidy. The new build structures are unbelievably sophisticated and high tech. It's like wandering into a James Bond film set. There is some very serious money there and it's oddly out of kilter with the apparent isolation of an remote island group.
The under ocean tunnels are weird. The hundreds of millions they must have cost just to service a few hundred people is extremely odd.
I was blown away by the place but my overriding impression was that I was missing something.

replies.author: @Beach_comber
replies.text: I wondered about the tunnels.  The four undersea tunnels cost a total of roughly $400 million.  At the latest count there are 55,466 Faroese.  That's a bit under $100,000 per head of population.  I've read that 81% of this was financed by British and American pension funds in exchange for bonds, with the remaining 19% paid by the Faeroes government, which also gave payment guarantees.  The interest on the bonds comes from the tolls paid to use the tunnels.  The numbers seem to work out.  I think the point is that the alternative: having no road connections, is so awful that people are happy to pay the tolls.  I had expected a big subsidy from Denmark or the EU would be involved, but apparently not.  In fact I've just been reminded that the Faroes aren't in the EU, even though they're not independent of Denmark.
